recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Future requests for missing or revised individual external terminology records, such as an old national ICD-10 variant URI or ICPC-1-NL identifier, should go through THO/UTG or TSMG review rather than FHIR core source.
issue_request: FHIR-6629 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Vocabulary change request asking the FHIR Code Systems page to define system URIs for WHO ICF, national ICD-10 variants for the US/Germany/Netherlands, and Dutch ICPC-1, with OID information where known.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit e2e7b1ea09020c8286800fc4fc62451eb5df21e7, matching Jira's svn revision 6372 comment. That commit added explicit ICD-10 variant, ICPC-1/ICPC-1-NL/ICPC-2, and ICF-NL rows to source/terminologies-systems.html; later ICD-specific commits moved and refined the ICD details.
additional_context: FHIR-37853 later established THO as the authoritative source of truth for external terminology identifiers and removed external rows without local FHIR usage pages, including the old ICPC and ICF rows. Current source/terminologies-systems.html is active and links to THO External Code Systems for authoritative external URI/OID details. Later ICF work in FHIR-37402, HTA-89, and UP-335 split international ICF from ICF Dutch translation, so the original ICF-NL/OID row would now be stale if restored to core.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source files were changed because the current core page already reflects the later approved THO-delegation policy, and re-adding FHIR-6629's old external rows would conflict with FHIR-37853.
